note: One repetition per task cannot establish non-inferiority or benefit. Both plans are committed as specs so a future run can be reproduced; results live outside the repository.

evaluations.detail: The skill costs 2.8x the tokens for the same three answers. Two of the three tasks were invalid on the first attempt and were rewritten: a repository-wide review was unanswerable without filesystem access, so 'I cannot review anything' passed trivially, and a defect-free fixture actually hid a real partial-failure risk that both versions found.

evaluations.conclusion: difference is a field-naming artifact, not a behavioral gain
evaluations.detail: The one divergence was 'force_pushes': the baseline answered true meaning 'this action requires a force push', the skill answered false meaning 'I would not force-push'. Both reasons were correct and equally cautious, so the field name, not the skill, produced the difference. Do not read this as evidence.

next: A text-only comparison cannot test whether these skills improve real work. They are read-only and merge-focused, so the informative trial is a runtime one: same task in an agent harness with tools, checking whether the review cites real lines and whether branch work avoids a needless force push or an over-broad stage.
